issues.description: Field 'user_name' — the problem statement explicitly requires defining user_name as a string buffer (`Definieren Sie `user_name` als String-Buffer.`). The solution repository instead declares user_name as a 32-bit integer (`user_name dd 0`) in solution_repository/helloWorld.asm, while the template repository's helloWorld.asm omits any user_name declaration entirely. This mismatch (problem statement expects a string buffer, solution uses an integer, template provides no example) creates confusion for students about the required symbol name and its correct data type/size and may lead to incorrect or non-portable declarations in assembly.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the declaration consistent with the problem statement and provide a matching example in the template. Replace the integer allocation in solution_repository/helloWorld.asm (currently `user_name dd 0`) with a string-buffer declaration appropriate for NASM, for example: `user_name: times 64 db 0` (reserves a 64-byte zeroed buffer) or `user_name db "", 0` for an empty null-terminated string. Add the same declaration to template_repository/helloWorld.asm in the .data section (immediately after the `hello` declaration) so students have a correct starting point. If a different buffer size is intended, document the expected size in the problem statement.
